A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same visible-thermal ordinality method despite the changed title. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and supplemental material are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original decomposition experiments, expert ordinality validation, quantitative benchmark comparisons, and loss ablations in Section 5, plus qualitative results in the appended figures.

after.justification: v2 retains original decomposition experiments and adds controlled-material ordinality validation and an illuminance sensitivity experiment in Section 3.5 and the supplement.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same visible-thermal edge and point-pair constraints, reconstruction and hinge losses, and two-network Double-DIP optimization with fixed random inputs. The shortened label definitions and reformatted loss equations do not establish an algorithmic change.

E1.justification: v2 adds controlled ordinality evaluation on 20 material samples under sunlight and white LED, and tests a color chart across varying illuminance. The principal datasets and decomposition task remain unchanged. Naming VT-Intrinsic and disclosing 600 pairs does not establish that all those scenes were newly added.

E2.justification: v2 Table 1 adds Opt-LocalSmooth across the quantitative benchmarks and NIR-Priors on incandescent and sunlight color-chart cases. RGB-Retinex gains comparisons on MIT Intrinsic and the authors' color chart, beyond its existing JoLHT-Video comparisons. Supplemental figures also add NIID-Net alongside retained learning baselines. JLHT-Video and JoLHT-Video refer to the same comparator.

E3.justification: The new material experiment varies sample orientation and lighting and obtains expert labels across patches. The new illuminance experiment varies incandescent-lamp distance, measures illuminance with a light meter, and evaluates albedo si-MSE. Existing benchmark metrics and the 100-scene, 20-pair expert-validation protocol are retained; newly stated optimization budgets are disclosures, not demonstrated setting changes.

E4.justification: v2 adds targeted tests of two central applicability questions: whether ordinalities survive variation in material properties, and how decomposition accuracy depends on illumination strength (Section 3.5 and supplementary Figure 10). These substantially extend the robustness evidence. The DDIP ablation and illustrated failure cases already existed in v1; their relocation and regrouping are not new analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random-seed controls, confidence intervals, significance tests, or error bars. The retained filtering by expert annotation confidence does not constitute new statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v2 adds material-validation accuracies of 98.59% under sunlight and 96.82% under white LED, the decreasing-error illuminance curve, additional baseline scores, and qualitative comparisons. Retained benchmark values are unchanged apart from equivalent rounding; MIT albedo/shading errors remain 0.019/0.005 and scene-level ordinality accuracy remains 98.95%. The without-DDIP color-chart score of 0.039 from v1 Table 2 is no longer tabulated, although its Painted-Mask results are retained.

T1.justification: The image-formation equations, heat-transport approximation, ordinal propositions, and proofs are substantively retained. The two proofs move into the supplement, heat-source notation changes, and v1 Assumption 1 becomes v2 Proposition 3 with the same statement and supporting approximation. These changes do not introduce a new mathematical result.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains decomposition from one visible-thermal pair without learned priors. v2 explicitly promotes VT-Intrinsic as a dataset contribution, claims robustness beyond ideal Lambertian conditions, and broadens the abstract's superiority claim from learning-based models to physics-based methods as well. This last claim needs qualification because JoLHT-Video retains lower errors on its dataset.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations connecting illumination strength to thermal SNR and material-validation results to robustness beyond ideal assumptions. The hydrant example gains an explanation involving low emissivity and poor thermal SNR, beyond v1's specularity discussion. Most limitations persist, but v1's explicit inability to handle multiple colored illuminations is omitted.

D1.justification: v2 newly reports approximately 5,000 iterations with DDIP and 500 without, runtimes of one minute and five seconds on an RTX 4090, the 600-pair dataset size, and the material list. Conversely, it omits v1's explicit input normalization to [0,1], reflected-boundary sampling, and normalization of estimated differences for the ordinal loss. These are documentation changes, not established implementation changes.

R1.justification: v2 adds a thermal-vision subsection covering geometry, materials, and appearance, and expands references supporting material validation, datasets, and optimization baselines. It also emphasizes NIR methods' limitations under LED lighting. RGB-Retinex's citation changes from Land and McCann to Hordley et al., without establishing an implementation replacement. The central positioning relative to joint light-heat transport remains intact.

P1.justification: v2 extensively rewrites and reorganizes the narrative: it changes the title, creates a dataset section, moves expert validation into the theory section, presents quantitative evaluation before qualitative evaluation, and combines limitations with the conclusion. Proofs and expanded supporting discussion are organized into a structured supplement.

P2.justification: v2 replaces the opening example with a method-pipeline figure, expands the illusion figure with edge and point-pair visualizations, and replaces the standalone road-edge illustration with a dataset montage. Three benchmark tables are consolidated into one categorized table, the ablation table gains a DDIP column, and new material and illuminance displays accompany extensively rearranged supplemental comparisons.

improvement.justification: The controlled-material validation, illuminance sweep, and additional physics and optimization comparators strengthen an already supported empirical case, while runtime disclosure improves transparency. These are useful but bounded gains. They are partly offset by omitted implementation details, broader superiority wording despite JoLHT-Video's lower errors, and inconsistent overcast-illuminance values between the supplementary discussion and Figure 10 caption.
